chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That Ali (peace be upon him) cut off the thief (of buried treasure).

key_terms.قَطَعَ: He cut off (referring to the hand)
key_terms.نَبَّاش: A person who digs up and steals buried treasure

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a nabbash according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this incident to establish the specific application of *qat' al-yad* (hand amputation) for *al-nabbash*, a thief who excavates buried treasure (*kanz*) from the earth. This narrative is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing the ruling of digging up hidden wealth from standard theft, emphasizing that the act of extraction itself triggers the fixed punishment. The report underscores the Imam's judicial authority in defining the scope of hudud punishments regarding property rights in Islamic law.
